automation_name: AI Security Wiki Topic News Collector

cutoff_window.date_policy: Only source records with an explicit publication timestamp strictly after the cutoff and no later than the run time qualify. Date-only, ambiguous, future-dated, and boundary-only records are excluded. A later database modification timestamp is not used to qualify an item.

searched_topics: agent and tool security, including MCP, plugins, browsers, delegated authority, and autonomous action
identity, authentication, authorization, credentials, and least privilege
model, dataset, dependency, artifact, runtime, cloud, hardware, and deployment supply chains
threat modeling, red teaming, security evaluation, assurance, monitoring, and release gates
AI security standards, regulation, governance, audit evidence, and risk management
public AI security incidents, mitigations, patches, disclosures, and lessons learned

wiki_and_routing_context.routing_rule: This downstream wiki retains the security finding, affected boundary, mitigation, and operating implication. Broad product, framework, and AI-development-practice background remains upstream-owned.

qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: NVD public CVE record with linked GitHub Security Advisory
qualifying_findings.summary: Coder 2.10.0 through before 2.34.8 exposes an unauthenticated local agent-debug endpoint whose manifest can disclose template-provided environment values, including cloud and registry credentials, to a lower-privileged process in the same workspace.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: Coder 2.10.0 to before 2.34.8; loopback agent debug server on port 2113.
qualifying_findings.ai_security_relevance: A coding-agent workspace crosses a local-process trust boundary into credential disclosure.

upstream_routing.note: Keep the agent-workspace credential boundary locally; route general Coder product background upstream.

qualifying_findings.follow_up: Confirm the advisory remediation and upgrade guidance during ingest.

qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: NVD public CVE record with linked project advisory, fix commit, and release
qualifying_findings.summary: OneUptime 14.0.2 through before 14.0.69 incorrectly applies project-wide permissions to cluster-scoped AI actions, allowing an authenticated member to invoke AI access tests, agent resets, kubectl-plan approval, incident AI conversations, or commands against clusters outside its scope.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: OneUptime 14.0.2 to before 14.0.69; Kubernetes AI and agent actions.
qualifying_findings.ai_security_relevance: This is a least-privilege failure where an AI-enabled operational control plane can cross tenant or cluster authorization boundaries.

upstream_routing.note: Retain the authorization and autonomous-operations implication locally; general OneUptime coverage is upstream-owned.

qualifying_findings.follow_up: Verify the release's exact fixed-build scope before durable synthesis.

qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: NVD public CVE record with linked remediation commit and release
qualifying_findings.summary: LobsterAI before 2026.10.16 uses a hard-coded password and salt to encrypt exported provider API keys; anyone obtaining the export can derive the AES-GCM key and recover third-party provider credentials.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: LobsterAI before 2026.10.16; exported provider-key backup files.
qualifying_findings.ai_security_relevance: The weakness exposes credentials that authorize model-provider use and therefore compromises the AI application credential boundary.

upstream_routing.note: Keep the credential-export control failure locally; route general LobsterAI product context upstream.

qualifying_findings.follow_up: Capture the project's replacement key-management behavior during ingest.

visible_dates.modification_note: The observed modification timestamp is after this run and is not used for qualification.

qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: NVD public CVE record with linked project issue
qualifying_findings.summary: YOLOE's AutoBackend model-loading path dynamically evaluates model-controlled values such as imgsz, names, and kpt_shape, permitting local code execution from a malicious model artifact; no maintained fixed release is identified.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: THU-MIG yoloe through commit 40cd606cabdbe2b566d6f14a6b162c89206e9a1b; AutoBackend model loading.
qualifying_findings.ai_security_relevance: It is a model-artifact supply-chain risk: loading an untrusted model can become code execution.

upstream_routing.note: Retain the unsafe model-loading security boundary locally; broad YOLOE background remains upstream-owned.

qualifying_findings.follow_up: Validate the exploit and upstream response before treating it as a general model-loading control.

visible_dates.modification_note: The observed modification timestamp is after this run and is not used for qualification.

qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: NVD public CVE record with linked project issue and public proof-of-concept reference
qualifying_findings.summary: AUTOMATIC1111 stable-diffusion-webui through 1.10.1 permits code injection through the Target value processed by its model-instantiation path; the record states a public exploit and no project response.
qualifying_findings.ai_security_relevance: Untrusted model configuration crosses directly into executable runtime behavior, a deployment and artifact supply-chain boundary.

upstream_routing.note: Keep the model-artifact execution finding locally; product catalog coverage belongs upstream.

qualifying_findings.follow_up: Recheck the project issue and fixed-version status during ingest.

visible_dates.modification_note: The observed modification timestamp is after this run and is not used for qualification.

qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: NVD public CVE record with linked remediation commit
qualifying_findings.summary: Xinference through 4.0.1 accepts Windows backslash traversal in custom model names, allowing an unauthenticated caller to register a persisted model that writes or deletes JSON configuration or data files reachable by the service process.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: Xinference through 4.0.1 on Windows; custom-model registration endpoint.
qualifying_findings.ai_security_relevance: An unauthenticated model-management API can alter runtime configuration and data, compromising the AI serving control plane.

upstream_routing.note: Keep the model-serving control-plane exposure locally; general Xinference material remains upstream-owned.

qualifying_findings.follow_up: Identify the first released fixed version before durable guidance.

qualifying_findings.summary: YOLOv9's DetectMultiBackend ONNX metadata handling can evaluate attacker-controlled names or stride values, enabling remotely exploitable code injection; the record reports public exploit availability and no vendor response.
qualifying_findings.ai_security_relevance: This is an untrusted-model-metadata execution risk, so model artifacts require supply-chain validation before inference loading.

upstream_routing.note: Retain the model-metadata execution implication locally; general YOLOv9 details belong upstream.

qualifying_findings.follow_up: Find the project issue or patch and reconcile overlap with other YOLO model-loader findings.

qualifying_findings.summary: Google OSS Agent Mesh (SAM) alpha releases have two related authorization defects: an unauthenticated libp2p peer can bypass Biscuit capability enforcement to invoke registered backend services, and a remote actor can self-enroll through the MCP proxy/OIDC registration path then invoke tools across connected MCP backend nodes.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: CVE-2026-102503: 0.1.0-alpha.1 through alpha.2; CVE-2026-103091: 0.1.0-alpha.1 through alpha.8.
qualifying_findings.ai_security_relevance: The cluster breaks authentication and delegated-authority enforcement across a mesh that reaches command, stdio-backed MCP, A2A, inference, and tool backends.

upstream_routing.note: Keep the mesh enrollment, tool invocation, and capability-policy implications locally; route broad Agent Mesh product coverage upstream.

qualifying_findings.follow_up: Obtain the linked project advisories and exact remediation releases before synthesis.

qualifying_findings.summary: Apache Answer through 2.0.2 lets holders of a global API key retrieve hidden, deleted, or pending-review answers through its MCP answer-retrieval tool; Apache recommends upgrading to 2.0.3.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: Apache Answer through 2.0.2; MCP answer-retrieval tool; fixed in 2.0.3.
qualifying_findings.ai_security_relevance: A global credential bypasses content-state authorization at an MCP data-retrieval boundary.

upstream_routing.note: Retain the MCP data-authorization control locally; route general Apache Answer background upstream.

qualifying_findings.follow_up: Verify the Apache advisory and release notes during ingest.

qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: NVD public CVE records; ESPnet record links a patch commit
qualifying_findings.summary: HanLP's classpath-driven model configuration loader and ESPnet's _target_-driven inference model handler each deserialize attacker-controlled configuration during model loading. The ESPnet record identifies patch commit f217b24f06de55e332cab10231469d5890dbbe00.
qualifying_findings.ai_security_relevance: Both are model/configuration supply-chain findings: a model-load input can become code execution in an inference environment.

upstream_routing.note: Keep the shared model-loader control implication locally while preserving separate products for eventual leaf routing.

qualifying_findings.follow_up: Verify HanLP remediation and split the two products during ingest if both remain independently actionable.

qualifying_findings.summary: llSourcell Doctor-Dignity's MLC Chat module allows code injection through the model_lib argument passed to python/mlc_chat/chat_module.py; the record reports public exploit availability but no versioned fix.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: Doctor-Dignity rolling-release revisions identified in the CVE; MLC Chat model_lib loader.
qualifying_findings.ai_security_relevance: A model-library selection field acts as an execution boundary, making untrusted model/runtime artifacts an AI supply-chain risk.

upstream_routing.note: Retain only the model-loader execution lesson locally; general project information is upstream-owned.

qualifying_findings.follow_up: Locate reproducible project evidence and fixed-state information before durable synthesis.

qualifying_findings.summary: AI Engine for WordPress before 3.7.9 fails object-ownership authorization for AI media actions, letting Editor-level users delete arbitrary protected posts or modify/change the type of arbitrary posts that they are otherwise not allowed to edit.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: AI Engine WordPress plugin before 3.7.9; AI media-management actions.
qualifying_findings.ai_security_relevance: AI-mediated content-management tools must enforce the same per-object authorization as their non-AI paths.

upstream_routing.note: Keep the AI-action authorization implication locally; general WordPress plugin background belongs upstream.

qualifying_findings.follow_up: Check plugin release notes and avoid duplicating ordinary WordPress coverage during ingest.

exclusions.reason: The record mentions agents only as one possible use of a generic bytecode library; it is not AI-specific.

exclusions.reason: Keyword matches are hardware or generic software contexts without a concrete AI-system security delta.

exclusions.reason: No directly retrievable primary CERT-In advisory with a reliable in-window publication/update timestamp was confirmed in this run.
Later modification timestamps cannot be treated as evidence available at this run; only their already in-window explicit publication timestamps were used where stated.

confidence_notes: NVD records are concrete public vulnerability evidence, but several model-loader records are NVD-first disclosures with no confirmed vendor fixed release; they remain medium confidence pending primary-project reconciliation.
The later-than-run NVD modification timestamps recorded for some findings were observed in a later database response and are explicitly non-qualifying metadata.

The two Google OSS Agent Mesh CVEs were grouped because both concern mesh enrollment/capability enforcement and were published seconds apart; ingest should decide whether their remediation paths require separate leaves.
follow_up_actions: During ingest, re-fetch vendor advisories, commits, and release notes for fixed-version wording before promoting NVD-first items to durable pages.
Split grouped CVE records where their affected surface or remediation differs materially.
Keep only the security lens in this repository and route general product/entity coverage to the federated upstream owner.
Do not move this artifact to raw/processed until normal source-to-wiki ingestion and independent verification succeed.
collection_blockers: NVD rate-limited individual-record enrichment after several successful requests; captured search responses and earlier record responses provide the stated public evidence.
Several vendor/project advisories were not independently fetched in this run and require ingest-time reconciliation.
